summary: Tested access-code gate, per-driver long-term memory, history screen and auth on all routes. Backend: new tests/test_iter21_auth_memory.py, 29/29 pass. These cover 401 on every non-public OpenAPI route without a token or with a bad token, wrong code -> 401, lowercase/whitespace code accepted, 5 wrong per X-Forwarded-For -> 429 while another IP still gets in, memory kept separate per driver, a fact from session A recalled in session B, DELETE clears it and it stays forgotten afterwards. Regression subset test_truckbuddy + test_onboarding: 25/25 pass. Frontend (390x844): access screen, wrong code error, 'truck2026' -> onboarding -> Skip -> map all work. Token persists across reload. An invalid or removed token sends the user back to the access screen. History flow works: empty state, typed 'find me a truck stop' sets a route (Sapp Bros) and both turns show in history, Clear (window.confirm accepted) empties it, Back returns with the route still shown. All 31 /api requests carried a Bearer token. Found and fixed 1 bug: reloading on /history, then tapping Back, did nothing ('GO_BACK was not handled' toast). No deprecated Expo packages detected.

minor.issue: Security: the per-IP limiter keys on the FIRST X-Forwarded-For entry, which the client controls. Spoofing it gets around the 5-per-IP limit (proven by test_rate_limit_429_after_5_wrong: a different XFF still got 200). Only the global ceiling of 100 then applies.

DoS risk: once anyone sends 100 wrong codes in 10 min, the global ceiling returns 429 to EVERY caller, including drivers with the correct code. New drivers are locked out for 10 minutes (services/auth.py:37).
The _attempts store is in-process memory: it resets on restart and is not shared across workers.
Public, so anyone can see the full API surface. Consider disabling them in production.

'Remembers forever' really means storage only. The agent context loads just the last MAX_HISTORY*2=16 turns (services/agent.py:218), so facts older than about 8 exchanges are not recalled. Also, the driver id is random on every code redemption, so clearing storage or switching device starts a new empty memory and leaves the old rows orphaned in Mongo.

ui_bugs.issue: Reloading the page or deep-linking to /history, then tapping Back, did nothing: router.back() with an empty stack shows the 'GO_BACK was not handled' error toast. FIXED: canGoBack() ? back() : replace('/'). Verified.

issues: Newest-first ordering shows the copilot reply ABOVE the driver question it answers, so each exchange reads upside down. Consider oldest-first with an inverted FlatList, or grouping by exchange.
The avatar image is a blank circle on first paint for a moment (image loads late). Minor.

action_items: auth.py: use the trusted (rightmost, ingress-added) X-Forwarded-For hop, or request.client, instead of the first entry.
auth.py: stop the global wrong-attempt ceiling from blocking correct codes, or use per-IP exponential backoff instead of a global lockout.

Optional: make long-term recall cover more than the last 16 turns (e.g. summarise older turns or extract facts). Decide how memory should work across devices and reinstalls (a new token means a new driver id).
Optional: history list ordering UX; disable /api/docs and /api/openapi.json in production.
critical_code_review_comments: services/auth.py:33-38: the per-IP limiter trusts the client-controlled XFF[0], and the global 100 ceiling then 429s correct codes for everyone.
server.py:131: session_id is prefixed with the driver id, so sessions are isolated across drivers. Good.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows after history-back fix

seed_data_creation: None persistent; test drivers' memory deleted in fixture teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Access code TRUCK2026. conftest.py patches requests to always send a token. To send NO token, pass headers={'Authorization': None}. Use a unique X-Forwarded-For per test to avoid tripping the rate limit. Every browser_automation run is a fresh context: enter the code, then Skip onboarding.
rca_of_issue: history-back: router.back() has no stack entry after a web reload or deep link to /history, so the GO_BACK action goes unhandled. Mitigation applied: fall back to router.replace('/').
